# Best Video Asset Management Software for Creative and Post-Production Teams (2026 Picks)

![Silhouette of a camera on a crane arm against an orange sunset, with trees and the setting sun below](https://www.orangelogic.com/hubfs/hero-camera-crane-1.91.jpg)

Quick Takeaways

- **Orange Logic:** best overall. Choose it if you need post-production tools and enterprise governance on one platform.
- **Frame.io:** best for review and approval. Choose it for active projects, especially in Adobe-centered workflows.
- **iconik:** best for a production-focused MAM. Choose it if you want to start on a published per-user plan
- **Avid MediaCentral:** best for Avid shops. Choose it if your broadcast or post team is built around Media Composer and Avid storage.
- **CatDV:** best for storage-centric video teams. Choose it for a video catalog managed close to your shared storage, especially Quantum's.

Choosing video asset management software comes down to how much of the workflow you want one system to own. Some teams need a review tool for cuts in progress, others need a searchable library for years of footage, and some want one platform shared with marketing and legal. Where your footage lives and which editing software you use narrows the field from there.

To help you narrow it down, we start with the capabilities that separate these tools in day-to-day post-production work. Then we compare five leading platforms and match each one to the teams it fits best.

## **What should creative and post-production teams look for in video asset management software?**

The best video asset management software connects to your editing tools, finds moments inside footage, and keeps rights attached from first cut to final delivery. Teams are investing to get there. In a January 2026 [Forrester Consulting study commissioned by Orange Logic](https://www.orangelogic.com/dam-resources/forrester-report-reimagining-dam-for-the-modern-enterprise), 80% of 313 global decision-makers said they plan to increase investment in rich-media management technology over the next two years. With most teams planning to upgrade, it pays to test each platform against the questions below before you commit.

## **What is the best video asset management software in 2026?**

Orange Logic is the strongest choice for teams that want post-production tools and enterprise governance on one platform. The other four platforms are worth a look for narrower needs, such as client review and approval or cataloging footage on a facility’s own servers.

| **Platform** | **Best for** | **Notable strengths** | **Considerations** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Orange Logic** | Enterprise teams unifying video with all other content | Premiere Pro plugin, hybrid storage, conversational AI search, built-in rights management | Implementation takes planning; pricing not published |
| Krock.io | Client review and approval alongside a DAM | Free no-login reviewer comments, per-version comment history, NLE timeline integrations | Review tool rather than a library |
| ****Anchorpoint**** | Artists, designers and engineers versioning large creative files | Simplified Git, file locking, engine and design tool integrations | Manages work in progress, not finished-asset distribution |
| ****Frame.io**** | Review and approval on active projects | Frame-accurate comments, Camera to Cloud, Adobe app panels | Long-term library and rights usually need a separate DAM |
| ****iconik**** | Production teams that want an easy starter option | Cloud and on-premises storage, AI tagging, published entry pricing | Key features in higher tiers; setup takes expertise |
| ****Filestage**** | Video review and approval with internal and external stakeholders | Frame-accurate comments, version-by-version sign-off, audit trail of approvals | Review tool; pair with a DAM for storage and rights |
| ****Avid MediaCentral**** | Broadcast, news, and post teams on Avid | Media Composer integration, modular packages, newsroom tools | Strongest when the wider stack is Avid |
| ****CatDV**** | Video teams that manage media close to their shared storage | On-premises and cloud storage support, workflow automation, AI enrichment | Setup and administration; strongest with Quantum storage |

## Which video asset management software fits your team?

Find your team's situation in the left column to see which platforms fit best.

| **If your team…** | **Consider** |
| --- | --- |
| Works in film, TV, or streaming | Orange Logic, Avid MediaCentral |
| Does commercials or agency work | Frame.io, Orange Logic |
| Makes corporate or brand video | Orange Logic |
| Mainly needs review and approvals | Frame.io |
| Mainly needs to search years of footage | iconik, Orange Logic, CatDV |
| Needs one system from ingest to archive | Orange Logic, CatDV |

### **Orange Logic: best overall for enterprise creative and post-production teams**

Orange Logic’s [media asset management platform](https://www.orangelogic.com/products/media-asset-management) brings video production into the same governed platform as the rest of an organization's content. Footage and proxies live in one place with their metadata and rights, so a clip approved in post carries its context into marketing, distribution, and the archive. Orange Logic was named a Leader in [The Forrester Wave: Digital Asset Management Systems, Q1 2026](https://www.orangelogic.com/a-forrester-wave-leader-dam-2026), and in the [2025 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Digital Asset Management Platforms](https://www.orangelogic.com/orange-logic-named-as-a-leader-in-the-gartner-magic-quadrant).

The platform scales to libraries of tens of millions of assets, which matters for studios and brands with large libraries spanning decades of footage.

**Strengths**

- **Editing without the file shuffle.** Work from Premiere Pro through the Orange Logic plugin and stream massive files with File on Demand
- [Hybrid storage.](https://www.orangelogic.com/dam-platform/dam-hybrid-storage) Connect local production storage and cloud content to search, preview, and govern media across locations while high resolution originals stay where production needs them.
- **AI search inside footage.** Search speech, scenes, faces, and logos, then jump to the exact timecode where they appear.
- **Frame-accurate review.** Leave timecoded comments, compare versions, and invite outside reviewers to comment or approve without an account. Route approvals automatically through [production workflows](https://www.orangelogic.com/dam-platform/workflows), and run [talent approvals](https://www.orangelogic.com/dam-platform/talent-approval-selects) in the same place so agents can sign off easily.
- **Rights that travel.** Link music, talent, and footage to their agreements with [digital rights management](https://www.orangelogic.com/products/digital-rights-management), so those terms follow each cut through transcoding and publishing.

**Considerations**

- **Setup takes planning.** Orange Logic is configured around each team's workflows, so expect an implementation phase before rollout.
- **Pricing is quote-based.** Costs depend on configuration and scale, and there's no published price list.

[Penske Media Corporation](https://www.orangelogic.com/dam-case-studies/penske-media), home to _Variety_, _Billboard_, and _Rolling Stone_, uses Orange Logic to manage more than 9 million assets across 40 brands and 300+ live events a year. During rapid-response events like the Golden Globes, editors at each brand publish approved video and photos while the event is still underway. Role-based access lets outside partners work in the same platform without opening up the whole library.

### Krock.io: best for client review and approval alongside your DAM

[Krock.io](https://krock.io/video-proofing/) is a video review and approval platform for creative agencies, post-production teams, and in-house brand teams. Teams share a cut with one link, and clients leave frame-accurate feedback without creating an account.

**Strengths**

- **Free, no-login client review.** Reviewers comment and draw on frames for free, without signing up, so client feedback doesn’t stall at account creation.
- **Version history.** Each version keeps its own comment thread, so teams can track how feedback was handled from cut to cut.
- **Notes in the timeline.** Integrations with DaVinci Resolve, Premiere Pro, and Final Cut Pro send comments straight to the editor’s timeline.

**Considerations**

- **Built for review, not long-term storage.** Krock.io organizes work by project and review round, so teams that need structured metadata, rights tracking, and an archive pair it with a DAM.

### Anchorpoint: Best for version control of large creative and 3D files

[Anchorpoint](https://www.anchorpoint.app/) is a version control solution for artists, designers and engineers. It runs on Git but simplifies it for creative teams. Artists can commit and sync work in a few clicks without learning Git commands. Animation, game development, architectural visualization and CAD teams use it to track versions of large files like 3D scenes, image sequences and video.

**Strengths**

- **Built for creative files:** File locking, thumbnails and selective checkout let teams lock files, preview work and download only what they need.
- **Fits existing pipelines:** Plugins and integrations cover Unreal Engine, Unity, Godot, Blender, Photoshop, Cinema 4D and Maya. It works with GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps and other Git hosts.
- **Your storage, your choice:** Either use Anchorpoint's cloud solution or an existing Git or Lore server such as GitHub.

**Considerations**

- **Version control, not a full asset library:** Anchorpoint is built for work-in-progress files. It doesn’t add rights management, approval workflows or distribution to other channels, so teams often pair it with a DAM to manage finished assets.

### **Frame.io: best for review and approval on active projects**

Frame.io, owned by Adobe, is one of the most widely used review and approval tools in video production. It's designed for teams collaborating on in-progress edits.

**Strengths**

- **Footage from set.**Send camera media straight into a project with Camera to Cloud.
- **Adobe integration.** See and resolve notes inside Premiere Pro and After Effects through built-in panels.

**Considerations**

- **Built for active projects.**Frame.io organizes media by project rather than as a long-term library, so teams that need structured metadata and rights tracking often pair it with a DAM.
- **Storage counts toward your plan.** Frame.io plans include storage limits, so keeping finished projects there long term can push you into a higher tier.

### **iconik: best for a production-focused MAM**

iconik, from Backlight, indexes media across cloud and on-premises storage into one searchable library. AI tagging, transcription, and review run on top.

**Strengths**

- **MAM and review together.**Review, annotate, and manage assets in the same tool.
- **Transparent entry pricing.**Start on a published, per-user Starter plan.

**Considerations**

- **Costs vary by plan and usage.** Features like SSO and rights management sit in higher tiers, and storage and AI processing are billed on top of per-user fees.
- **Setup takes expertise.** Reviewers note a steep learning curve, and connecting iconik to your storage takes careful configuration.

### Filestage: best for video review and approval

[Filestage](https://filestage.io/) is a review and approval platform for creative, marketing, and compliance teams. Reviewers leave frame-accurate comments on videos, and teams approve each version with internal and external stakeholders in one place, with a full audit trail of every decision.

Strengths

- **Frame-accurate feedback:** comments sit on the exact frame they refer to.
- **Version approval:** every version goes through sign-off with internal and external reviewers.
- **Compliance-ready records:** approval tracking shows who approved which version, and when.

Considerations

- **Review-focused:** Filestage handles feedback and approval, so teams pair it with a DAM for storage and rights.

### **Avid MediaCentral: best for broadcast, news, and post teams on Avid**

Avid MediaCentral gives producers, assistants, and newsroom staff access to the same media Avid editors are cutting, often from a web browser. Teams typically start with the module they need most and add newsroom or asset management tools as they grow.

**Strengths**

- **Options by team size.** Start with Editorial Management for small and mid-size post teams, or scale to Production Management for large broadcasters.
- **Newsroom depth.** Plan each newscast's running order and manage story production in the same system your editors use.

**Considerations**

- **Works best on Avid.**MediaCentral fits best when your editors already work in Avid Media Composer and store media on Avid storage. Avid announced support for media in other clouds, such as AWS and Azure, in September 2026, so ask what's available today.
- **Add-ons drive the price.**MediaCentral is sold as a base package with separate add-ons for newsroom tools, media transfer, and asset management, so confirm which ones you need before comparing prices.

### **CatDV: best for video teams that manage media close to their shared storage**

Quantum CatDV is a video catalog designed to sit close to a facility's shared storage, and Quantum often sells it as a turnkey package with its own storage systems. That setup makes it a common choice for post-production teams that run their own on-site infrastructure.

**Strengths**

- **Works across storage.** Catalog media on local servers and cloud storage, including Azure, with proxy playback that doesn't require downloads.
- **Workflow automation.** Automate ingest, transcoding, and archive steps with CatDV's automation workers.

**Considerations**

- **Setup takes administration.**Deployments are usually configured by integrators or in-house media engineers, so plan for setup and ongoing upkeep.
- **Strongest with Quantum storage.** Many customers pair CatDV with Quantum's StorNext storage, so confirm how it fits your existing infrastructure.

## FAQs: Video asset management platforms

#### What is the difference between DAM and MAM?

DAM manages digital content of every type, while MAM adds features built for production media. Those include proxies for large files, frame-accurate review, and transcoding. Orange Logic runs both on one platform, so finished video moves into marketing and archive without a migration.

#### Can video editors work in the DAM without leaving Premiere Pro?

Yes. Platforms with a Premiere Pro plugin let editors search and place governed media from inside the editing environment. Orange Logic pairs its plugin with File on Demand streaming, so large files open without full downloads.

#### How does AI help with video asset management?

AI turns footage into searchable data. Speech-to-text, face recognition, and object detection let teams search for a spoken phrase or a person and land on the exact timecode.

#### When does a standalone video review tool make sense?

A standalone review tool makes sense when a team mainly needs fast feedback on active edits and already manages its library elsewhere. Frame.io is the best-known example. Once teams need rights tracking, long-term search, or reuse across departments, a DAM or MAM usually becomes the system of record.

#### How much does video asset management software cost?

Pricing models vary. Some tools charge per user, with storage and AI usage billed on top, while enterprise platforms usually quote based on configuration and scale. To compare fairly, add up seats, storage for originals and proxies, and implementation, then subtract the cost of any tools the new platform would replace.
